source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Three types of mites (MITES) damage citrus in this source: citrus red mite (ពីងពាងក្រហម, Panonychus citri, family Tetranychidae), which causes leaves and fruit rind to take on a dull, silvery-bronze stippled appearance from feeding punctures; citrus rust mite (ពីងពាងលឿង, Phyllocoptruta oleivora, family Eriophyidae), a tiny mite that causes a characteristic russeting/bronzing of fruit rind, reducing the fruit's market appearance even though the fruit inside is unaffected; and broad mite (ពីងពាងស, Polyphagotarsonemus latus, family Tarsonemidae), which distorts new leaf and shoot growth.

Mite populations tend to build up quickly in hot, dry conditions and can be worsened by broad-spectrum insecticide use that kills off the predatory mites and insects that would otherwise keep pest mite numbers in check.

Because rust mite damage is cosmetic (affecting rind appearance rather than fruit quality inside) while red mite and broad mite can affect tree vigor and new growth, the source recommends monitoring mite levels before treating, protecting natural predators where possible, and using a miticide only when populations are clearly damaging, rather than as a routine spray.
